outcome_law: y = 0.2 + 0.4 t1 + 0.3 t2 + 0.2 z, plus 0.01 sin(0.31 i) on the row index i

oracle.method: Closed form of the stated additive structural law. The tier closure {z} | {t1, t2} | {y} adjusts for z, so E[y | do(t1 = 1, t2 = 1)] = 0.2 + 0.4 + 0.3 + 0.2 mean(z); mean(z) = 660/960 = 11/16 from the exact cell counts, giving 83/80 = 1.0375. The wiggle 0.01 sin(0.31 i) is only asymptotically orthogonal to the design, which is what the posterior-mean tolerance covers.
asserted_outputs: level.value (the posterior mean is asserted within tolerance.posterior_mean)
oracle.independence_basis: The generator evaluates the stated additive law and the exact count average in rationals; it imports no Antecedent code and no statistics package. The shared object is the stated law and the design counts.
oracle.historical_exposure: Written for this fixture from the stated law and the declared inputs; no product implementation source was consulted to obtain the values.

reference_review.scope: The joint level of a same-tier do(t1 = 1, t2 = 1) under an additive law with a confounded design.
reference_review.independence_basis: The generator evaluates the stated additive law and the exact count average in rationals; it imports no Antecedent code and no statistics package. The shared object is the stated law and the design counts.
reference_review.historical_exposure: Written for this fixture from the stated law and the declared inputs; no product implementation source was consulted to obtain the values.
reference_review.redistribution: Repository-authored MIT OR Apache-2.0 generator and deterministic inputs. Python standard library only, in an isolated locked script environment, outside the product and ordinary CI; no upstream source is stored.
reference_review.limitations: The additive law is the specification of the Bayesian cell's outcome regression; for a law with a treatment interaction the published level is the additive model's level, not the saturated cell mean, and this fixture does not speak to that. Law-level truth, no interval or calibration claim.
